title: Quantization Profile Library — draft notes (schema + open questions)
body:
Last updated: 2025-03-08 (Arjun)

This is a working doc / scratchpad for Quantization Profile Library. Contains:
- early schema draft(s)
- naming + versioning debates
- hardware/compatibility representation ideas
- links to early benchmark artifacts + eval notes
- TODO list + owners

Not canonical. Canonical docs will move to Confluence once we settle the v1 surface.

---

0) TL;DR / current leaning (as of 2025-03-08)
- Profiles are versioned, immutable artifacts referenced by a stable ref string.
- Route-level config selects a profile ref or "default" (baseline). No tenant-wide default in v1 (ADR-0137).
- Runtime selection must be deterministic given (route config, resolved model variant, region/tier, hardware class).
- Compatibility checks live in policy engine (control plane) and are duplicated as runtime guardrails (belt+suspenders). Fallback always to baseline precision.
- Publishing policy: profile lifecycle is author->validate->publish (staged)->deprecate->remove (removal only when no routes reference + grace period).

---

1) Goals & non-goals (raw notes)
Goals
- stable schema for describing quantization configuration per model variant
- ability to pin a profile for safety / reproducibility
- route-level enablement + region/tier constraints
- evaluation + quality guardrails (block publishing / block enablement where needed)
- observability: know if applied vs fallback vs disabled per request

Non-goals (v1)
- per-customer auto-recommendation ("turn it on automatically")
- on-the-fly auto-tuning in prod
- default-on across all routes/models

---

2) Terminology (still inconsistent in threads)
- profile_id: unique identifier for an immutable profile record (may include version)
- profile_ref: what customers/config refer to (string) -> resolves to a concrete profile_id
- alias: e.g. "recommended" or "latest". Concern: silent changes.
- baseline: default precision path (whatever model variant ships with)

Notes from Slack (eng-ml/1739211042)
- People keep conflating profile_id vs profile_ref. If we choose to expose aliases, we need strong semantics + audit logging. Ethan strongly prefers explicit pinning for GA.

Current draft stance
- Expose explicit versioned refs by default.
- Optional aliases for internal canaries only (or behind allowlist). If we ever expose aliases to customers, require explicit opt-in + change notifications.

---

3) Early schema draft (v0.3-ish) — NOT FINAL
This is a strawman. Expect to simplify.

3.1) Top-level shape (stringly typed pseudo-schema)
- schema_version: "1.0"
- profile_id: "qp_<model>_<variant>_<method>_<yyyymmdd>_<hash>" (immutable)
- display_name: human-readable name
- status: "draft" | "validated" | "published" | "deprecated" | "revoked"
- model_id: registry model id (e.g. "llama3-70b")
- model_variant: variant id (e.g. "llama3-70b-instruct-v3")
- quant_method: "gptq" | "awq" | "smoothquant" | "fp8" | "int8" | "mixed" (we’ll likely constrain)
- weights:
  - dtype: "int8" | "int4" | "fp8_e4m3fn" | "fp8_e5m2" | "fp16" (note: baseline may still be fp16/bf16)
  - group_size: "128" | "64" | "none"
  - granularity: "per_channel" | "per_tensor" | "block"
- activations:
  - dtype: "int8" | "fp8_e4m3fn" | "bf16" | "fp16"
  - scheme: "static" | "dynamic"
- kv_cache:
  - dtype: "fp16" | "bf16" | "fp8" | "int8" (runtime team wants guardrails)
  - notes: freeform
- calibration:
  - dataset_ref: "calset://<name>@<version>" (internal)
  - sample_count: string int
  - prompt_set_refs: comma-separated refs (if used)
  - date_range: "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD"
- constraints:
  - hardware_classes: "h100" | "a100" | "l40s" | "t4" | etc
  - min_driver: "550.x" (string)
  - min_cuda: "12.1" (string)
  - max_context_tokens: string int
  - max_batch_tokens: string int (optional)
  - sequence_length_regime: "short" | "mixed" | "long" (hand-wavy, not great)
- expected_impact:
  - cost_token_delta_pct: e.g. "-18%" (string)
  - p95_latency_delta_pct: e.g. "+3%"
  - vram_delta_gb: e.g. "+0.6"
- known_caveats: list-ish text (or markdown-like bullets)
- quality_summary:
  - eval_suite_refs: "eval://quant-regression@v2" etc
  - pass_fail: "pass" | "fail" | "borderline"
  - max_allowed_delta: reference to policy doc
- artifacts:
  - artifact_uri: "s3://.../profiles/<profile_id>/..."
  - checksum: sha256
  - signature: (we should have signing; see registry PR-18358)
- created_by, created_at, last_validated_at

This is too much for v1 if we expect to publish dozens of profiles; might split into:
- profile metadata (small)
- validation report (bigger, internal)

3.2) Example (for discussion only)
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "profile_id": "qp_llama3-70b_llama3-70b-instruct-v3_int8w-fp16a_20250227_5a1c",
  "display_name": "INT8 weights / FP16 activations (H100/A100)",
  "status": "published",
  "model_id": "llama3-70b",
  "model_variant": "llama3-70b-instruct-v3",
  "quant_method": "int8",
  "weights.dtype": "int8",
  "weights.group_size": "128",
  "activations.dtype": "fp16",
  "kv_cache.dtype": "bf16",
  "calibration.dataset_ref": "calset://redwood-mix-v5@2025-02-20",
  "calibration.sample_count": "2048",
  "constraints.hardware_classes": "h100,a100",
  "constraints.max_context_tokens": "8192",
  "expected_impact.cost_token_delta_pct": "-14%",
  "expected_impact.p95_latency_delta_pct": "+2%",
  "known_caveats": "Slight degradation on math-longform prompts; avoid >8k context on A100-40G",
  "artifacts.artifact_uri": "s3://redwood-registry/profiles/qp_llama3-70b_.../artifacts.tar.zst",
  "artifacts.checksum": "sha256:..."
}

Yes, this example is ugly. That’s the point: we need to decide what’s first-class vs what’s internal-only.

---

4) Open decisions / unresolved questions

4.1) profile_ref vs profile_id vs aliases
- Option A: Only allow explicit versioned profile_id in route config.
  Pros: no silent behavior changes; deterministic; easy audit.
  Cons: more painful to adopt; customers have to update config to get improvements.

- Option B: Allow profile_ref with aliases ("recommended", "latest") that resolve server-side.
  Pros: fewer customer actions; can roll improvements quicker.
  Cons: silent changes = scary; can break reproducibility; needs strong comms + “pin on read” UX.

Current leaning: route config stores an explicit versioned ref (customer picks). We can support a Console UX button “upgrade to latest recommended” which writes a new explicit ref and creates an audit event.

Slack reference: eng-platform/1741073409 (avoid silent changes without customer action)

4.2) Where do compatibility rules live?
- Policy engine (control plane) must block incompatible enables. But runtime still needs guardrails because:
  - cached config / propagation delays
  - misconfig / manual overrides
  - mixed hardware pools

Proposal: compatibility evaluated in control plane returns “resolved_quant_mode” + “resolution_outcome” enum, and runtime verifies the resolved mode is supported on node; if not, runtime falls back + increments fallback counters.

Need to decide: do we “hard fail” or “fallback”? For v1: fallback always, but emit a loud signal.

4.3) Representing hardware constraints
We currently hand-wave “hardware_classes”. Runtime wants more specific:
- GPU SKU (h100-sxm vs h100-pcie?)
- compute capability
- supported kernels list (int8 GEMM path vs fp8 etc)
- driver + cuda min

But too much specificity makes profiles brittle across regions. Maybe a middle layer:
- hardware_class: {"hopper", "ampere", "ada"}
- gpu_vram_gb_min
- compute_capability_min

TODO: talk to Hiro/Noah about what minimal contract runtime can support without a combinatorial explosion.

4.4) KV cache dtype and long-context behavior
From eng-runtime/1739305589 + 1740217732: KV cache interactions can cause surprising memory + perf deltas.
- If profile changes kv_cache dtype, does that need to be encoded in the profile explicitly (yes?)
- What about per-seq-len thresholds? e.g. allow INT8 weights but only under max_context 8k.
- Do we need separate profiles per context regime?

Open: how do we validate long-context regressions without making eval suite too expensive?

4.5) Quality gating: what blocks publish vs what blocks enable?
We have two choke points:
- publishing into library
- enabling on a route

Edge case: profile is “published” but only allowed for certain customers (design partners) while we learn.
Do we represent that as:
- status=published but allowlist at control plane
- status=validated but “private”

We need a consistent story for Console:
- show “Experimental (allowlisted)” vs “Generally available”
- block enabling unless route is allowlisted (or unless tenant has feature flag)

4.6) What do we expose to customers?
- Do customers see calibration dataset refs? Probably not.
- Do customers see benchmark deltas? Probably yes but must be caveated: workload-dependent.
- Do customers see known caveats? yes.
- Do customers see max_context caps? yes (hard constraints).

---

5) Links to early benchmarks / artifacts

5.1) Benchmark summary publishing
- benchmark-lab PR: github://benchmark-lab/pr-18623-publish-cost-token-deltas-for-profile-library
- internal artifact locations (placeholders, may move):
  - s3://redwood-benchmark-lab/quant-profiles/weekly/2025-02-28/summary.csv
  - s3://redwood-benchmark-lab/quant-profiles/weekly/2025-02-28/latency_p95_by_gpu.csv
  - s3://redwood-benchmark-lab/quant-profiles/weekly/2025-02-28/vram_delta_by_profile.csv

Notes
- We need a stable artifact URI scheme that survives refactors.
- Ideally profile points to a validation report artifact, which includes:
  - hardware matrix test results (pass/fail)
  - perf deltas
  - quality results
  - runtime version used

5.2) Early results (hand-copied; do not quote externally)
(“cost/token delta” is estimator; not final billing numbers)
- llama3-70b-instruct-v3 INT8(w)/FP16(a)
  - H100: cost/token ~ -12% to -16% depending on batch; p95 decode +0-3%; VRAM +0.4GB
  - A100-80G: cost/token ~ -9% to -13%; p95 decode +2-6% at long seq
  - Risk: slight quality hit on “math-longform” prompt set; borderline in week-1

- mixtral-8x7b-instruct FP8-ish mixed path (experimental)
  - H100: cost/token ~ -18% but kernel path unstable under some seq len distribution
  - Runtime asked to cap to <=4k until kernel guardrails land

TODO: Jonas to paste in more precise numbers once bench CSVs are in a stable location.

---

6) Notes from quality guardrail discussions (Selene + Sana)
- We need a publish gate that uses quantization regression thresholds (Confluence policy).
- For borderline cases, we should support "blocked" state + explicit comment + a link to eval run.
- Statistical questions:
  - do we require paired tests on same prompts? yes for A/B harness.
  - minimum sample sizes differ by task family.

Practical note: we should avoid making “publish gate” too slow.
Potential approach:
- “fast gate” suite (small) required for all profiles
- “full gate” suite required before marking “GA-ready”

We need to encode in metadata whether a profile is "experimental" vs "stable".

---

7) Control plane / route config notes (from Ethan / Priya sync)
- Route config field likely: quantization_profile_ref
  - Values: "default" OR "<explicit profile ref>"
- Control plane resolves:
  - resolved_profile_id (or empty)
  - resolution_outcome: applied | fallback_incompatible | fallback_disabled | error
  - compatibility_reason (string enum; used for UI + logs)

RBAC: only route admins can change; must emit audit log diff.
Console should show preview: “This profile is compatible with your selected region/tier: Yes/No” with link to compatibility matrix.

---

8) Runtime integration concerns (Noah / Hiro)
- Determinism: given same resolved_profile_id, runtime must select same kernel path. Avoid “auto choose” heuristics that can change between builds without versioning.
- Cache interactions:
  - prefix/KV caching may be invalidated by dtype changes
  - need to tag cache entries by quant_profile_id to avoid mixing
- Observability:
  - request logs/traces should include quant_profile_id + outcome
  - metrics: applied_rate, fallback_rate, incompatible_enable_attempt_rate

---

9) TODOs / owners (living list)

Schema
- [ ] Decide minimal v1 metadata vs internal-only fields (Arjun + Quentin) — target 2025-03-15
- [ ] Pick naming convention: profile_id format + stable ref format (Arjun + Ethan) — 2025-03-12
- [ ] Decide how to represent hardware constraints without SKU explosion (Hiro + Noah + Arjun) — 2025-03-18

Quality / evals
- [ ] Define “fast gate” vs “full gate” suites (Selene + Jonas + Sana) — 2025-03-20
- [ ] Document what “borderline” means + how to override/block (Selene) — 2025-03-22
- [ ] Add route-level A/B harness toggle support check (Olivia) — in progress (see eval-harness PR)

Bench artifacts
- [ ] Agree on stable artifact URI scheme + retention (Jonas + Nadia + SRE) — 2025-03-25
- [ ] Build a tiny summary format we can show in Console (Nadia + Chloe) — 2025-03-28

Runtime
- [ ] Confirm cache keying strategy includes quant_profile_id (Omar + Noah) — 2025-03-19
- [ ] Enumerate kernel guardrails for mixed fp8/int8 (Hiro) — 2025-03-21

Control plane + Console
- [ ] Confirm what error message customers see when enabling incompatible profile (Ethan + Chloe) — 2025-03-14
- [ ] Confirm audit log fields needed for compliance exports (Naomi + Kevin) — 2025-03-26

---

10) Random notes / parking lot
- Should we allow profile to specify “requires runtime >= X”? (Probably yes; we’ve been burned by kernel regressions.)
- Deprecation flow: if a profile is found to regress quality on a new prompt set, do we “revoke” it? If revoked, control plane should prevent new enables and prompt existing users to move; what about already-enabled routes? (likely: continue but warn? or force fallback?)
- If we add a kill-switch (global disable), does profile metadata need to know about it? no, but Console messaging should.

---

Appendix A: meeting notes (rough)

2025-02-21 (Applied ML + Runtime) — “determinism + caching”
- Runtime wants: quant_profile_id in traces and cache keys.
- Applied ML wants: ability to publish multiple profiles per model variant (e.g., int8 for H100, different for A100).
- Action: Arjun to propose constraints encoding; Noah to propose runtime guardrail list.

2025-03-05 (Beta prep check)
- Need to ensure “feature off => absolutely unchanged behavior.”
- Decide allowlist mechanism for design partners.
- Establish rollback criteria: fallback_rate spike, p95 decode regression, quality trigger.

(End)
